title: Phase 0 · Clear the ground
description: One repository from QTOS's history; QQ, ARQADE and QOR Media carried with theirs; the QOR core at a pinned commit; one rulebook and decision log; shared CI runners. Exit: qor-os builds and tests in CI on Windows and Linux, the carried products included on Windows.

title: Phase 1 · One stack
description: QQ, ARQADE and QOR Media on Linux as Wayland clients of Prism; QTOS.Input drives QQ; Lumen tokens theme every app; a controller-first Home and Library. Exit: Orb Run plays inside Prism on Linux with a DualSense, and Linux CI runs the products' suites.

title: Phase 2 · Identity and keys
description: The vault as a system service from the QOR core, with approvals drawn by Prism; one QOR ID sign-in; Social and the Library index in the shell. Exit: sign in once, chat in World, and publish Orb Run on the devnet from QQ Studio inside Prism.

title: Phase 3 · Boots and plays PC games
description: The Fedora Atomic image (bootc, NVIDIA open modules, Mesa); Prism's own KMS backend (every display at its own refresh on every GPU, VRR, direct scan-out); Steam and Proton in gamescope; greeter; updates with rollback; real daemons and sandbox. Exit: the reference laptop boots QOR OS at 360 Hz on its panel and 60 Hz on a television, and plays a Steam game and Orb Run.

title: Phase 4 · The ecosystem
description: The public SDK, one catalogue for the Store and the Market, the Store's developer program, the premium shell features. Exit: an outside developer ships a QQ game to QOR OS using only the public SDK.
